text: Over 570 enterprises attend Vietnam-Southwest China Strategic Development Connectivity Forum

General Secretary of the Communist Party of Vietnam Central Committee and President To Lam attended the Vietnam-Southwest China Development Strategy Connectivity Forum that opened in Kunming, Yunnan province, on November 20, as part of his China trip for the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Week and bilateral activities, the Vietnam News Agency reported.

According to the organizers of the forum, this is the largest-ever forum connecting Vietnam with Southwest China, attracting more than 800 registered participants from 570 businesses of the two countries.

Addressing the forum, General Secretary and President Lam congratulated Yunnan on its socio-economic development achievements, particularly in green industries, high technology and specialised agriculture.

He expressed his confidence that the province will successfully realise the strategic goals set by General Secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and President Xi Jinping and the CPC Central Committee, becoming a model of ethnic solidarity and progress, a pioneer in ecological civilisation and ecological security protection, and a gateway to South Asia and Southeast Asia.
He noted that Vietnam and Southwest China have complementary strengths.

Southwest China has a vast market and increasingly strong industrial and innovation capabilities, while Vietnam boasts a dynamic economy, extensive international integration and seaports connecting it to major global shipping routes.
By bringing into full play these advantages, the two sides can create shared development opportunities, linking inland areas with the sea, China with Southeast Asia and both with global markets.
Welcoming the initiative to organise the forum, the Vietnamese leader said that strategic connectivity will help each side unlock its development potential and create opportunities for partners.
He called for cooperation with broad-reaching impact, turning geographical proximity into a competitive advantage and further strengthening ties between the two countries' people.
He shared that his talks with General Secretary and President Xi during this visit produced positive and practical outcomes.
Looking ahead, he urged both countries to further promote their extensive cooperation mechanisms while placing greater emphasis on mutual benefits.

General Secretary and President Lam called on localities from both sides to strengthen policy, infrastructure, economic, trade, science and technology connectivity, as well as people-to-people exchanges.

He also encouraged Southwest China's localities and businesses to enhance cooperation and make quality investments, thereby fostering shared market development and strengthening each other's capabilities.
The top Vietnamese leader showed his belief that political trust, determination at all levels and business innovation will help usher in a deeper and more effective phase of cooperation.
He also called for making the most of the 2026-2027 Vietnam-China Tourism Cooperation Year to connect heritage routes and promote exchanges among people and young generations.
According to statistics from the organizing committees of both countries, enterprises have registered 58 memoranda of understanding (MOUs) for signing at the forum.
Areas of interest include logistics services, air and rail transportation, energy, industrial park investment, agricultural products, food processing, and cross-border import-export trade.

Vietnamese businesses expect the forum to help address bottlenecks in infrastructure and logistics services, thereby reducing transportation costs, expanding markets for agricultural products and fruits, and identifying technology partners and funding sources for renewable energy, mineral processing, and manufacturing industries.

On the Chinese side, enterprises from Yunnan Province are interested in expanding their presence in the Vietnamese market with key products such as green aluminum, silicon photovoltaic products, new-energy batteries, rare metals, and basic chemicals.
